description: STAR LIGHT, NASA Space Apps Challenge yarışmasına katılmak üzere bir araya gelen, bilime, teknolojiye ve uzay araştırmalarına ilgi duyan beş kız ortaokul öğrencisinden oluşan bir takımdır. Meraklarını yaratıcılıkla, fikirlerini teknolojiyle birleştiren takımımız, uzayın sonsuz keşif yolculuğunda yenilikçi çözümler üretmeyi hedeflemektedir. Çünkü biz, geleceği aydınlatacak beş küçük yıldızız!
summary: Last Signal is a 3D educational game, built in Unity, in which players design, manage and simulate a complete lunar mission. Players first investigate a real mission, the 2025 Athena (IM-2) landing, then plan their own search for water ice at the Moon's south pole as Captain BESİBA: they choose a landing region, select instruments within mass and budget limits, and drive a VIPER-inspired rover while managing energy and communications. When a mission fails, a "Mission Traces Log" shows which decision caused the failure, so players can improve the plan and try again. The game turns abstract engineering trade-offs into choices with visible consequences. Our motto: "Every mistake is the map of the next mission."
details: WHAT IT DOES The Last Signal follows one loop: learn from a real mission, design your own, test it, and improve it. 1. 2025 - Learn from Athena. An opening cinematic shows the Athena (IM-2) lander touching down and tipping over, so its TRIDENT drill cannot operate. The player inspects the lander, reads fact cards, and plays a Safe Landing Simulation comparing landing zones with different surface slopes. 2. 2026 - Design the mission. In a simulation center the player controls Captain BESİBA, a Turkish woman astronaut. At the map table they choose one of three regions: a sunlit ridge (safer, less science), a crater rim (medium risk) or a dark crater (most promising for water ice, highest risk). At the rover platform they pick from six instruments under a 70 kg mass limit and a budget limit, and see a mission forecast before launch. 3. 2027 - Test it on the Moon. The player drives a VIPER-inspired rover across the lunar surface. Sunlight and shadow, line-of-sight to Earth for signal, cold, battery level and slope are all simulated. The player follows a hydrogen trace, drills, and must transmit the data before energy or signal runs out. 4. Learn from failure. If the battery dies, the rover freezes, tips over or loses contact, the mission ends with "Mission not completed, but you gained new knowledge." The Mission Traces Log lists the decisions and what went wrong. The player returns to the design screen and tries a better plan. A successful mission is scored on six criteria and compared with earlier attempts. HOW IT ADDRESSES THE CHALLENGE Every decision costs one of four resources: Energy, Budget, Mass or Communication. No plan is perfect: the site with the highest science value is the least safe. Players experience a full mission from concept to operation and see how each choice shapes the outcome. SCIENTIFIC HONESTY Real NASA information carries a red "REAL NASA MISSION" label and fictional parts carry a blue "FICTIONAL SIMULATION" label, so players always know which is which. Water ice is never shown as crystals; it appears as hydrogen data measured by a spectrometer. There is no sound in vacuum: the player hears only vibration through the rover body and radio tones. TOOLS Unity 6 (URP), C#, the new Input System, and a WebGL build that runs in the browser. All sounds and music are generated in code. The game is available in Turkish and English, for school-age students. TEAM Betül, Esma, Sara, İpek and Buğlem. BESİBA's name is formed from our initials plus "Ay", the Turkish word for Moon. Five names. Five traces. One signal.
